<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:aspire" data-paper-title="ASPIRE: Asynchronous Batch Self-Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-aspire-a1351704" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ede71e564dc50d74">Why choose drafts per request?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aaspire">ASPIRE: Asynchronous Batch Self-Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Online acceptance and remaining conditions vary. Use current batch cost and per-request statistics, with periodic refresh for state correction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A frequent long-draft accepter need not match a frequent rejecter&#x27;s length.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17943">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.17943-aspire/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ede71e564dc50d74">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:aspire" data-paper-title="ASPIRE: Asynchronous Batch Self-Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3be38b55eeb6ffa7">Why let ASPIRE choose draft lengths independently within a batch?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aaspire">ASPIRE: Asynchronous Batch Self-Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Requests differ in acceptance and remaining state. One length can waste checks or lose gains. Use batch costs and periodic full-attention refresh for self-speculation. Local tests do not modify a full engine.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Give different lengths to frequently accepted and first-token-rejected requests, while accounting for shared batch cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17943">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.17943-aspire/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3be38b55eeb6ffa7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:aspire" data-paper-title="ASPIRE: Asynchronous Batch Self-Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3e520f7e53219a96">Is per-request choice the same as ignoring batch and acting greedily?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aaspire">ASPIRE: Asynchronous Batch Self-Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Decisions still use shared batch costs; ignoring resource and synchronization effects changes the scheduler.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Longer drafts can benefit one request but increase group verification cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17943">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.17943-aspire/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3e520f7e53219a96">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:aspire" data-paper-title="ASPIRE: Asynchronous Batch Self-Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-fcb5b7f9ae76d071">Does the local ASPIRE scheduler and refresh gate constitute a vLLM integration?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aaspire">ASPIRE: Asynchronous Batch Self-Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Verify real scheduling, cache handoff, refresh execution, and time separately. A reference schedule is not deployment throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A log showing draft length eight does not prove asynchronous service execution or correct KV transfer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17943">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.17943-aspire/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fcb5b7f9ae76d071">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:data-space-iteration" data-paper-title="Few-Step Generation via Data-Space Iteration" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-data-space-iteration-cef25f24" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-48133a6bbe3428ba">What changes across Data-Space Iteration refinements?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adata-space-iteration">Few-Step Generation via Data-Space Iteration</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance Seed</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A shared network updates data predictions from fixed noise. Iteration counts refinement, not the separate DMD noising time τ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Refinement three is another prediction update, not diffusion time three.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12102">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.12102-data-space-iteration/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-48133a6bbe3428ba">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:data-space-iteration" data-paper-title="Few-Step Generation via Data-Space Iteration" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-039b91ebbdf6cbe4">Why refine with the same noise rather than interpreting iteration index as flow time?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adata-space-iteration">Few-Step Generation via Data-Space Iteration</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance Seed</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The shared generator repeatedly improves one data-space prediction from fixed original noise. DMD uses frozen real teacher and fake distribution model. Earlier refinements are detached and only the current one trains; it is not real-image regression. Local tiny runs do not replace paper metrics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Refine outline then detail from the same noise; changing noise or time semantics changes the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12102">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.12102-data-space-iteration/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-039b91ebbdf6cbe4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:data-space-iteration" data-paper-title="Few-Step Generation via Data-Space Iteration" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e76cd9b0d0ef4e4b">Is direct real-image regression equivalent to DMD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adata-space-iteration">Few-Step Generation via Data-Space Iteration</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance Seed</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. DMD uses a frozen real teacher and a fake model fitted to generated data to supply a distribution-matching direction. Per-step paired image regression replaces it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A teacher-minus-fake direction on a generated sample is not assigning a fixed real image to noise.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12102">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.12102-data-space-iteration/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e76cd9b0d0ef4e4b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:data-space-iteration" data-paper-title="Few-Step Generation via Data-Space Iteration" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-718c6f2b28293a39">How isolate prefix, fake model, and generator gradients?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adata-space-iteration">Few-Step Generation via Data-Space Iteration</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ByteDance Seed</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Roll out prefix without a graph and train the final refinement. Train fake on detached samples; freeze teacher/fake gradients during generator updates and detach the direction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Updating step four does not backpropagate through the first three steps or teacher.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12102">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.12102-data-space-iteration/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-718c6f2b28293a39">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dblast" data-paper-title="DBLast: Dependent Block Drafting for Stochastic Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-dblast-5689bd49" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-dafbe6dd11decfb4">Why can individually likely draft positions form a poor block?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adblast">DBLast: Dependent Block Drafting for Stochastic Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Technologies Canada</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Independent proposals ignore joint dependencies. DBLast conditions on a shared latent, inducing correlation without abandoning parallelism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Common colors and objects can still combine incoherently if chosen independently.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05448">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.05448-dblast/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dafbe6dd11decfb4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dblast" data-paper-title="DBLast: Dependent Block Drafting for Stochastic Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f6c6be038ac0c88f">How does DBLast&#x27;s shared latent address independent parallel draft positions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adblast">DBLast: Dependent Block Drafting for Stochastic Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Technologies Canada</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Given one latent, positions can sample in parallel; marginalizing it yields dependence across positions. Optimize expected verification length, not isolated hits. Target verification still matters and local mechanism is not service speed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One latent can coordinate singular/plural choices instead of independently picking inconsistent words.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05448">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.05448-dblast/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f6c6be038ac0c88f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dblast" data-paper-title="DBLast: Dependent Block Drafting for Stochastic Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2df450592211aa64">How does a latent mixture differ from independent unigram proposals?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adblast">DBLast: Dependent Block Drafting for Stochastic Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Technologies Canada</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Independent proposals multiply marginals. DBLast multiplies conditional probabilities under the same z and integrates z, so identical marginals can have different joints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Both positions can be half A/B, with only AA and BB or with all four pairs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05448">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.05448-dblast/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2df450592211aa64">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dblast" data-paper-title="DBLast: Dependent Block Drafting for Stochastic Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-41a53700b992ffab">Why check exact speculative acceptance instead of position hit rate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adblast">DBLast: Dependent Block Drafting for Stochastic Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Huawei Technologies Canada</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Benefit depends on accepted contiguous prefix and joint quality. Isolated correct positions need not pass as a block. Local Markov target and rank-four proposal are mechanism tests, not real throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Correct first and third tokens do not help the third if the second is rejected.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05448">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.05448-dblast/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-41a53700b992ffab">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:doublecat-semicat" data-paper-title="On the Design Space of Continuous Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-doublecat-semicat-01018306" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5c0323d9b9c7012e">Why reveal some tokens as clean one-hot vectors early?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adoublecat-semicat">On the Design Space of Continuous Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Oxford / Apple（在 Apple 期间完成）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>High-dimensional Gaussian noise can swamp a norm-one signal. Revealed anchors remain fixed, while loss covers unrevealed positions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Confirmed words stay clean as other positions denoise.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13834">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13834-doublecat-semicat/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5c0323d9b9c7012e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:doublecat-semicat" data-paper-title="On the Design Space of Continuous Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-d81c0b5a5fbc8665">Why are DoubleCat two-level interpolation and SemiCat permanent reveal distinct?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adoublecat-semicat">On the Design Space of Continuous Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Oxford / Apple（在 Apple 期间完成）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Interpolation shifts training toward interior simplex states to reduce endpoint mismatch. Permanent reveal leaves chosen tokens clean and fixed, supervises unrevealed positions, and adjusts hazard to remaining time. Neither adds default self-conditioning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keeping a confirmed subject clean differs from training on interior probability patterns.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13834">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13834-doublecat-semicat/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d81c0b5a5fbc8665">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:doublecat-semicat" data-paper-title="On the Design Space of Continuous Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-102a07e552e2b869">Does two-level interpolation require an extra denoiser call for self-conditioning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adoublecat-semicat">On the Design Space of Continuous Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Oxford / Apple（在 Apple 期间完成）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Interpolation constructs inputs without another denoiser. SemiCat also needs no default extra call. Optional bootstrap self-conditioning is a separately costed ablation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not hide a second forward under a nominal one-call training budget.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13834">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13834-doublecat-semicat/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-102a07e552e2b869">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:doublecat-semicat" data-paper-title="On the Design Space of Continuous Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6986d7d1c325c468">How test final hazard one together with permanent carryover?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adoublecat-semicat">On the Design Space of Continuous Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Oxford / Apple（在 Apple 期间完成）</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>At the last step reveal all remaining positions. Preserve already revealed inputs and outputs at every step. Use untempered probabilities for continuous Euler and temperature only for categorical commits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A token revealed at step two cannot change at step three.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13834">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13834-doublecat-semicat/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6986d7d1c325c468">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dqwen35" data-paper-title="dQwen3.5: Adapting Hybrid Language Models into Bidirectional Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-dqwen35-77ccc4a5" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8797f4eb60febff3">Why convert a hybrid backbone into a bidirectional diffusion LM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adqwen35">dQwen3.5: Adapting Hybrid Language Models into Bidirectional Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Texas at Austin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Masked denoising uses visible context on both sides rather than causal next-token prediction. Attention and recurrent paths, and the objective, all change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A masked middle word can use left and right words.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20751">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.20751-dqwen35/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8797f4eb60febff3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dqwen35" data-paper-title="dQwen3.5: Adapting Hybrid Language Models into Bidirectional Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-628204eccd8870fd">Why does bidirectional dQwen3.5 need more than removing an attention mask?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adqwen35">dQwen3.5: Adapting Hybrid Language Models into Bidirectional Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Texas at Austin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The hybrid backbone also has recurrence. Both state propagation and attention must support bidirectional context for masked denoising. Running a propagation kernel does not establish a fully adapted checkpoint or loss curve.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A sentence-start blank can need the end; changing only attention leaves recurrence one-way.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20751">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.20751-dqwen35/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-628204eccd8870fd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dqwen35" data-paper-title="dQwen3.5: Adapting Hybrid Language Models into Bidirectional Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a0ecca512c918406">How does masked bidirectional visibility differ from autoregressive training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adqwen35">dQwen3.5: Adapting Hybrid Language Models into Bidirectional Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Texas at Austin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>AR is prefix-causal; denoising can use visible left and right context. Adapt the hybrid state path and do not assume causal cache equivalence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A known word after a blank is legal evidence for denoising but not next-token AR.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20751">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.20751-dqwen35/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a0ecca512c918406">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dqwen35" data-paper-title="dQwen3.5: Adapting Hybrid Language Models into Bidirectional Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b58767fde4bdf527">Why test both attention and recurrence for bidirectional conversion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adqwen35">dQwen3.5: Adapting Hybrid Language Models into Bidirectional Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Texas at Austin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Removing the attention mask can leave recurrence one-way. Local CUDA only confirms component execution, not a 9B checkpoint or full denoising curves.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Right context reaching one branch does not make the other bidirectional.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20751">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.20751-dqwen35/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b58767fde4bdf527">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:echo" data-paper-title="ECHO: Early-layer Collaborative Hierarchical Orchestration with Bonus Logits in Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-echo-675d4c78" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-cf24dec53cc5f9b0">Why explore frequently in early layers but verify less often at the end?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aecho">ECHO: Early-layer Collaborative Hierarchical Orchestration with Bonus Logits in Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Wuhan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Early proposals are cheap; full depth verifies reliably. Dual loops and bonus logits expand candidates while aiming to reduce waits and preserve corrected sampling.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Let the light path expand promising branches for full-depth checking.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17241">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.17241-echo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cf24dec53cc5f9b0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:echo" data-paper-title="ECHO: Early-layer Collaborative Hierarchical Orchestration with Bonus Logits in Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bdd24109fa6354ee">Why not use ECHO bonus logits as the final sampling distribution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aecho">ECHO: Early-layer Collaborative Hierarchical Orchestration with Bonus Logits in Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Wuhan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Frequent cheap early proposals and less frequent authoritative late checks cooperatively expand the candidate tree. Exploration may differ from the target and requires exact rejection correction. Local candidate/tensor checks do not measure throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A bonus branch may enter verification without being accepted automatically.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17241">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.17241-echo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bdd24109fa6354ee">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:echo" data-paper-title="ECHO: Early-layer Collaborative Hierarchical Orchestration with Bonus Logits in Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-339dbce0d5c7dcc9">Why separate exploration scores from target sampling?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aecho">ECHO: Early-layer Collaborative Hierarchical Orchestration with Bonus Logits in Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Wuhan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Bonus logits serve proposals and expansion. Exact rejection correction maintains the target distribution. Sampling bonuses directly changes behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Trying a favored candidate first does not entitle it to higher final probability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17241">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.17241-echo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-339dbce0d5c7dcc9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:echo" data-paper-title="ECHO: Early-layer Collaborative Hierarchical Orchestration with Bonus Logits in Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d65f387fa303137c">How does candidate merge validation differ from CUDA throughput evidence?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aecho">ECHO: Early-layer Collaborative Hierarchical Orchestration with Bonus Logits in Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Wuhan University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reference verifies merge and lossless correction; A100 receipt verifies the tensor path. Real speed needs early/late scheduling, caching, and measured time.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Distribution parity does not prove ideal GPU overlap.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17241">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.17241-echo/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d65f387fa303137c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:langdit" data-paper-title="Designing Transformers for Continuous Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-langdit-ba73a77f" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e37db734cbc08d6b">Why add a likelihood shortcut besides noisy embeddings?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alangdit">Designing Transformers for Continuous Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dots Studio, Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Codebook-to-noisy-state relations supplement token posterior with noise-conditioned backbone and bounded calibration. This is more than a normal head and needs correct gradients and self-conditioning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>At low noise, nearby codebook vectors help identify the underlying token.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22330">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22330-langdit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e37db734cbc08d6b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:langdit" data-paper-title="Designing Transformers for Continuous Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-999cd9aaee6ecf4c">Why detach only the explicit codebook shortcut, not the entire noisy input?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alangdit">Designing Transformers for Continuous Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dots Studio, Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Both paths share a codebook. Detaching shortcut gradient still lets the codebook learn through noisy input; detaching everything breaks it. Training uses entropy-gated self-conditioning while inference uses unweighted posterior mean.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Freeze one shortcut multiplication, not the same table&#x27;s input construction path.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22330">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22330-langdit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-999cd9aaee6ecf4c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:langdit" data-paper-title="Designing Transformers for Continuous Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-11b5da4d78a813dc">Should training entropy gating also weight inference posterior means?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alangdit">Designing Transformers for Continuous Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dots Studio, Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Training bootstrap confidence-attenuates and detaches feedback. Inference uses unweighted pC and no extra bootstrap. Training heuristics are not posterior guarantees.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not discount inference probability mass a second time because training suppressed low-confidence feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22330">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22330-langdit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-11b5da4d78a813dc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:langdit" data-paper-title="Designing Transformers for Continuous Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a19870609b8abb9b">Why initialize calibration aψ to one and constrain it to [0.5,2]?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alangdit">Designing Transformers for Continuous Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Dots Studio, Xiaohongshu</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One preserves initial shortcut scale. Bounded exponential calibration avoids extreme amplification or suppression, with 5000 warmup steps. Verify ranges and gradient paths.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Large calibration outputs must not make the shortcut dominate the vocabulary head.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22330">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22330-langdit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a19870609b8abb9b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:loopspec" data-paper-title="LoopSpec: Pipelined Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-loopspec-856a7101" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ba81a43442fcdf04">Why is self-speculation natural for shared-block loops?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aloopspec">LoopSpec: Pipelined Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University / KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Intermediate depth provides draft predictions and deeper loops verify. This reuses model weights; pipelined residual proposals reduce intended waiting.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Draft with fewer loops, then verify with more.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17184">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.17184-loopspec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ba81a43442fcdf04">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:loopspec" data-paper-title="LoopSpec: Pipelined Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-2ca2ea44d8975e44">Why can LoopSpec use intermediate loop predictions without an independent drafter?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aloopspec">LoopSpec: Pipelined Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University / KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Shallower loop states give cheap predictions and deeper computation verifies them. Pipelined residual proposals aim to overlap waiting. Actual acceptance and scheduling determine gains; a reference scheduler does not measure GPU throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reusing shallow drafts saves a separate model but frequent rejection can erase benefits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17184">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.17184-loopspec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2ca2ea44d8975e44">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:loopspec" data-paper-title="LoopSpec: Pipelined Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-98ca8dd6b68a1879">What does LoopSpec reuse compared with an independent drafter?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aloopspec">LoopSpec: Pipelined Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University / KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It reuses intermediate predictions and shared loop structure, rather than a second parameter set and path. Speed still depends on proposal quality, verification, and scheduling.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Removing separate drafter weights does not ensure candidates are accepted.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17184">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.17184-loopspec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-98ca8dd6b68a1879">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:loopspec" data-paper-title="LoopSpec: Pipelined Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-980fa512cb80cf33">Does a depth scheduler establish real GPU pipelining?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aloopspec">LoopSpec: Pipelined Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Seoul National University / KAIST</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It checks proposal/depth transitions, not actual overlap, cache handoff, or verification execution. Planned concurrency is not measured throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A log claiming overlap cannot show synchronization did not serialize the GPU.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17184">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.17184-loopspec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-980fa512cb80cf33">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:medusa" data-paper-title="Medusa: Simple LLM Inference Acceleration Framework with Multiple Decoding Heads" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-medusa-8eb57905" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-700adaef304fe397">Why add multiple future-token heads to one hidden state?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amedusa">Medusa: Simple LLM Inference Acceleration Framework with Multiple Decoding Heads</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Together AI / Princeton University / University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different offsets provide multiple proposals at once. Tree verification can reduce sequential calls without removing backbone verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Propose t+1 and t+2 from h_t before checking accepted combinations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.10774">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2401.10774-medusa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-700adaef304fe397">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:medusa" data-paper-title="Medusa: Simple LLM Inference Acceleration Framework with Multiple Decoding Heads" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-91bfb6f20f55ba61">Why verify a candidate tree rather than concatenate each Medusa head&#x27;s top token?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amedusa">Medusa: Simple LLM Inference Acceleration Framework with Multiple Decoding Heads</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Together AI / Princeton University / University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Heads predict different offsets from the same state and may not form a valid autoregressive chain. A tree exposes combinations for backbone validation. Independent losses do not prove correctness or sampling guarantees, and local work has no GPU tree kernel.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Separately chosen nouns and verbs need not form a coherent phrase.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.10774">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2401.10774-medusa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-91bfb6f20f55ba61">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:medusa" data-paper-title="Medusa: Simple LLM Inference Acceleration Framework with Multiple Decoding Heads" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-ecbaa441479f51df">Why don&#x27;t fewer backbone calls imply the same percentage latency reduction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amedusa">Medusa: Simple LLM Inference Acceleration Framework with Multiple Decoding Heads</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Together AI / Princeton University / University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Extra heads, tree construction and validation, batch shape, kernels, and acceptance all matter. Mechanism call counts are not measured GPU speed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Halving calls may double the work per verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.10774">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2401.10774-medusa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ecbaa441479f51df">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:medusa" data-paper-title="Medusa: Simple LLM Inference Acceleration Framework with Multiple Decoding Heads" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-321b91366afe4f45">How align Medusa&#x27;s k-th head targets?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amedusa">Medusa: Simple LLM Inference Acceleration Framework with Multiple Decoding Heads</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Together AI / Princeton University / University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Predict x_{t+k} from h_t, matching slices and valid endpoints. One common next-token target would train duplicate offsets.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Head two at h_10 predicts x_12, not x_11.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.10774">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2401.10774-medusa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-321b91366afe4f45">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:pumba" data-paper-title="On Trajectory-Aware Training for Masked Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-pumba-d6ea4c98" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-142bd7ecbfaa617c">Why train on the model&#x27;s own progressive-unmasking trajectory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apumba">On Trajectory-Aware Training for Masked Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Independent noise may miss states reached by actual multistep sampling. Carry through self-generated unrolls exposes dependent decisions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Revealed words determine the next input rather than independently recreating noise.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37974">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.37974-pumba/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-142bd7ecbfaa617c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:pumba" data-paper-title="On Trajectory-Aware Training for Masked Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-295de760f5896ce6">Why propagate gradients across several PUMBA carry steps?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apumba">On Trajectory-Aware Training for Masked Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Carry affects future denoising, so isolated loss may not learn useful carry. Unroll on-policy reveals and backpropagate within fixed windows, truncating between windows for cost. Local work is not full diffusion LM training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Later fill-in errors should shape how earlier carry represents entity constraints.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37974">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.37974-pumba/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-295de760f5896ce6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:pumba" data-paper-title="On Trajectory-Aware Training for Masked Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3eb472980073a93b">How does trajectory-aware carry training differ from independent steps?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apumba">On Trajectory-Aware Training for Masked Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>BPTT lets later loss affect earlier carry. Independent examples cut those dependencies, and summing their CEs does not restore them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Step-two loss should influence step-one carry, not only local step-two computation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37974">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.37974-pumba/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3eb472980073a93b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:pumba" data-paper-title="On Trajectory-Aware Training for Masked Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6b958073b73e1c11">Should PUMBA detach carry every step or at window boundaries?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Apumba">On Trajectory-Aware Training for Masked Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Apple</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keep gradients through the fixed window and detach between windows. Per-step detachment removes the mechanism; fully untruncated training changes memory and protocol. Local reference did not train LLaDA-8B.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>At window length three, step three reaches two earlier steps in the same window only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37974">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.37974-pumba/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6b958073b73e1c11">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:r4t" data-paper-title="Efficient, Property-Aligned Fan-Out Retrieval via RL-Compiled Diffusion" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-r4t-4721c6f0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b8913b09736b8f3e">Why build a set-level alignment target before training a fast retriever?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ar4t">Efficient, Property-Aligned Fan-Out Retrieval via RL-Compiled Diffusion</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign / Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Item scores alone may not guarantee whole-set properties. Compile a composite set target into diffusion fan-out to seek fewer online steps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Relevant outputs should cover different evidence rather than repeating one top item.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.06397">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2603.06397-r4t/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b8913b09736b8f3e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:r4t" data-paper-title="Efficient, Property-Aligned Fan-Out Retrieval via RL-Compiled Diffusion" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-106925b5c8b75df1">Why align retrieval sets before compiling into a diffusion fan-out retriever?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ar4t">Efficient, Property-Aligned Fan-Out Retrieval via RL-Compiled Diffusion</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign / Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Set value includes coverage and diversity beyond item relevance. Define trade-offs with a composite set reward, then train fast diffusion retrieval to approximate it. Reward alignment may be imperfect; local work only implements the set objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Three individually relevant duplicates can be worse than a set covering separate facts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.06397">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2603.06397-r4t/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-106925b5c8b75df1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:r4t" data-paper-title="Efficient, Property-Aligned Fan-Out Retrieval via RL-Compiled Diffusion" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b272b8d4569a6c1a">How does set alignment differ from independent item ranking?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ar4t">Efficient, Property-Aligned Fan-Out Retrieval via RL-Compiled Diffusion</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign / Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sets account for relations and redundancy. Summing independent scores can miss coverage. The compiled retriever requires separate training and evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Three high-relevance duplicates can have low diversity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.06397">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2603.06397-r4t/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b272b8d4569a6c1a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:r4t" data-paper-title="Efficient, Property-Aligned Fan-Out Retrieval via RL-Compiled Diffusion" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-fc66c1b00e56a5d1">Does the local R4T component train the 53.9M diffusion retriever?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ar4t">Efficient, Property-Aligned Fan-Out Retrieval via RL-Compiled Diffusion</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign / Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It computes the alignment/diversity objective, without training the full generator. Scoring candidates is not generating fan-out results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A function ranking supplied sets cannot necessarily retrieve a set from a query.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.06397">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2603.06397-r4t/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fc66c1b00e56a5d1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:register-tokens-dllm" data-paper-title="Register Tokens for Bounded-State Reasoning in Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-register-tokens-dllm-e9299172" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
