<h2 id="qa-8c20693d27f0d551">Why use a fixed number of register tokens across diffusion chunks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aregister-tokens-dllm">Register Tokens for Bounded-State Reasoning in Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Wisconsin–Madison</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hidden states pass some earlier information after text is cleared, while bounding capacity. This is also an information bottleneck.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The next chunk gets several continuous vectors rather than all previous words.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16372">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.16372-register-tokens-dllm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8c20693d27f0d551">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:register-tokens-dllm" data-paper-title="Register Tokens for Bounded-State Reasoning in Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8ccfd44bd0885c4e">How can fixed registers support cross-chunk reasoning after text removal, and what is lost?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aregister-tokens-dllm">Register Tokens for Bounded-State Reasoning in Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Wisconsin–Madison</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Continuous hidden registers carry compressed previous-chunk information at fixed size. They do not preserve original text or guarantee fine detail. Train and evaluate retention; no complete local diffusion checkpoint.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A relationship can survive as state while an omitted name cannot be guaranteed recoverable.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16372">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.16372-register-tokens-dllm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8ccfd44bd0885c4e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:register-tokens-dllm" data-paper-title="Register Tokens for Bounded-State Reasoning in Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e3c98792dfdfe1ae">How does register carry differ from keeping all text or KV?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aregister-tokens-dllm">Register Tokens for Bounded-State Reasoning in Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Wisconsin–Madison</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Carry is a fixed-size continuous summary. Text/KV grows and permits finer position access. Fixed registers are not lossless compression.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two hundred pages still compress into eight vectors without expanding capacity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16372">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.16372-register-tokens-dllm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e3c98792dfdfe1ae">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:register-tokens-dllm" data-paper-title="Register Tokens for Bounded-State Reasoning in Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-ecf865b886448827">How verify old text is not retained through an undeclared bypass?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aregister-tokens-dllm">Register Tokens for Bounded-State Reasoning in Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Wisconsin–Madison</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Check that the next chunk receives only the agreed registers, clear old text and undeclared caches, and verify state updates. Local work omits LLaDA/Dream and diffu-GRPO.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Fixed register count is insufficient if the old text is secretly concatenated anyway.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16372">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.16372-register-tokens-dllm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ecf865b886448827">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:speculative-decoding" data-paper-title="Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-speculative-decoding-bd568875" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-18b195341bdbc8b6">Why can a small draft reduce large-target serial calls?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aspeculative-decoding">Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Draft proposes blocks and target verifies in a batch, advancing through the accepted prefix. Exact acceptance/rejection correction preserves the target distribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One target call can accept several candidates rather than one per call.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.17192">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2211.17192-speculative-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-18b195341bdbc8b6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:speculative-decoding" data-paper-title="Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bd026bc4bd6ddae3">Why sample positive residual after rejecting a speculative proposal?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aspeculative-decoding">Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Accepting by target/proposal ratio already contributes some target mass. Sample normalized positive target-minus-proposal remainder to fill the rest. Resampling target directly double-counts accepted mass. Local token transitions do not measure large kernels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>When draft overweights one word, residual correction fills undercovered alternatives.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.17192">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2211.17192-speculative-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bd026bc4bd6ddae3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:speculative-decoding" data-paper-title="Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d5c4d20915b086ea">Is greedy agreement the same guarantee as exact stochastic speculation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aspeculative-decoding">Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Greedy agreement preserves a deterministic argmax path. Exact stochastic sampling needs p/q acceptance and residual correction for the complete distribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Identical highest-probability words can hide different second- and third-choice probabilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.17192">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2211.17192-speculative-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d5c4d20915b086ea">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:speculative-decoding" data-paper-title="Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-54352a57f3453951">Why not commit later drafts unconditionally after a rejection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aspeculative-decoding">Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Their prefix included the rejected token. Correct the token, discard the invalid suffix, and continue from the new prefix. Local Markov call counts are not T5-XXL latency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If word two changes, words three to five cannot assume the old word two.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.17192">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2211.17192-speculative-decoding/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-54352a57f3453951">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:tadm" data-paper-title="Time-Anchored Diffusion Language Models: Latent-Space Caching for Fast Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-tadm-0fb9bc3b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-b887b96c6f1ca604">Why needn&#x27;t the expensive anchor run at every step?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atadm">Time-Anchored Diffusion Language Models: Latent-Space Caching for Fast Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Texas at Austin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Neighboring reverse steps can reuse part of the state. Refresh periodically and use cheap state-conditioned corrections in between before smaller denoising.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Several steps share one anchor but produce different corrections.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37924">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.37924-tadm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b887b96c6f1ca604">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:tadm" data-paper-title="Time-Anchored Diffusion Language Models: Latent-Space Caching for Fast Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0b7ec87ec23ca88a">Why gate corrections to TADM cached anchors based on current diffusion state?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atadm">Time-Anchored Diffusion Language Models: Latent-Space Caching for Fast Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Texas at Austin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reusing expensive latent outputs saves anchor calls, but changing states make anchors stale. A cheap conditioned fusion predicts and gates corrections for a smaller denoiser. It cannot guarantee full recovery, and local tests omit full generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Adjust an early rough sentence representation once later words become known.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37924">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.37924-tadm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0b7ec87ec23ca88a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:tadm" data-paper-title="Time-Anchored Diffusion Language Models: Latent-Space Caching for Fast Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5c0c8e549d5c34b5">How does gated stale-cache correction differ from reuse unchanged?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atadm">Time-Anchored Diffusion Language Models: Latent-Space Caching for Fast Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Texas at Austin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It combines c_t and the old anchor to adjust stale information. Refresh may still be needed; fusion is not an exact substitute for every anchor call.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A changed denoising state can revise old features instead of treating them as fresh.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37924">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.37924-tadm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5c0c8e549d5c34b5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:tadm" data-paper-title="Time-Anchored Diffusion Language Models: Latent-Space Caching for Fast Generation" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-f04d97a265814e48">What boundary checks validate TADM&#x27;s g and Δ fusion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atadm">Time-Anchored Diffusion Language Models: Latent-Space Caching for Fast Generation</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · The University of Texas at Austin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use h_t′+g⊙Δ. Zero g or zero Δ recovers the anchor, not zero. Local cache correction does not load DiffusionGemma-26B.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Turning the gate off keeps the original anchor.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37924">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.37924-tadm/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f04d97a265814e48">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:windowed-mtp" data-paper-title="Windowed-MTP: Removing the Full-Context Draft-KV Tax at Million-Token Context" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-windowed-mtp-ad617a2b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-f4622ee554153341">Why window only the draft?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Awindowed-mtp">Windowed-MTP: Removing the Full-Context Draft-KV Tax at Million-Token Context</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NVIDIA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Draft KV reads can bottleneck long contexts. Retain sinks and recent draft history while the full target verifies, changing proposal cost and acceptance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Draft might read recent 64 and a few sinks while target reads all 16K.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21535">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.21535-windowed-mtp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f4622ee554153341">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:windowed-mtp" data-paper-title="Windowed-MTP: Removing the Full-Context Draft-KV Tax at Million-Token Context" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-869f887ecd35e200">Why can shrinking only Windowed-MTP&#x27;s draft context save reads without changing the target distribution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Awindowed-mtp">Windowed-MTP: Removing the Full-Context Draft-KV Tax at Million-Token Context</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NVIDIA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Draft reads sinks and recent tokens; the full target still sees all history and corrects proposals. The window affects draft cost and acceptance, not the exact target definition. Cutting target context changes the guarantee; local latency does not transfer to production.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Target can reject a wrong draft caused by missing old evidence, provided its own history stays complete.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21535">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.21535-windowed-mtp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-869f887ecd35e200">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:windowed-mtp" data-paper-title="Windowed-MTP: Removing the Full-Context Draft-KV Tax at Million-Token Context" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e21f03e9bf00b0a4">Why doesn&#x27;t a large reduction in draft keys yield the same TPOT reduction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Awindowed-mtp">Windowed-MTP: Removing the Full-Context Draft-KV Tax at Million-Token Context</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NVIDIA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Draft forwards and target checks still cost time, and time per output depends on accepted length AL. Lower acceptance can offset savings.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Cheaper verification that accepts fewer tokens may yield little throughput gain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21535">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.21535-windowed-mtp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e21f03e9bf00b0a4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:windowed-mtp" data-paper-title="Windowed-MTP: Removing the Full-Context Draft-KV Tax at Million-Token Context" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-02f172d22260d687">Should overlaps between sinks and recent tokens duplicate KV?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Awindowed-mtp">Windowed-MTP: Removing the Full-Context Draft-KV Tax at Million-Token Context</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · NVIDIA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Use the union without duplicates. Only draft indices change; target retains the full cache.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A position in both sets appears once in draft attention.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21535">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.21535-windowed-mtp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-02f172d22260d687">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:b3" data-paper-title="Blurring the Block Boundaries: Overlapping Block Denoising for Efficient Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-b3-cde2b2be" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-d407deba409efb2a">Why must a shared forward pass prevent future drafts from affecting the current block?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ab3">Blurring the Block Boundaries: Overlapping Block Denoising for Efficient Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-11 · Technion / Amazon Web Services</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Block-causal attention blocks current-block queries from future keys/values. The future block may read the current block, not vice versa. Overlap then preserves the current block&#x27;s attention input, while the future sampler still needs self-editing as its prefix settles.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For two4token blocks in an8token attention matrix, the first4rows must not see the last4columns; the last4rows may see the first4columns.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 数据协议与代码映射. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14387v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2611.14387-b3/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d407deba409efb2a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:b3" data-paper-title="Blurring the Block Boundaries: Overlapping Block Denoising for Efficient Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f3ca0ee1b71a557b">Why use previous-pass entropy and strictly exclude the frontier token?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ab3">Blurring the Block Boundaries: Overlapping Block Denoising for Efficient Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-11 · Technion / Amazon Web Services</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The candidate estimates the solved region strictly left of the advanced frontier using the preceding pass. Including the frontier or using current-pass entropy changes the self-calibration sample. Candidates require an advancing frontier, no active future block and an available previous pass.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the new frontier is position2, use the previous pass&#x27;s maximum entropy over positions0and1, not position2 or the just-decreased current entropy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14387v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2611.14387-b3/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f3ca0ee1b71a557b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:b3" data-paper-title="Blurring the Block Boundaries: Overlapping Block Denoising for Efficient Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e425de57d5146b0d">Should very low current entropy always spawn another future block?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ab3">Blurring the Block Boundaries: Overlapping Block Denoising for Efficient Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-11 · Technion / Amazon Web Services</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. A calibrated candidate threshold must exist, no future block may already be active, and EOS must not be predicted. An active future block suppresses both spawning and candidate collection. Candidates carry across blocks, but the previous-pass entropy cannot be reused with another block&#x27;s positions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Even if maximum entropy is .01, an already active future block must not spawn a third block. Predicted EOS also suppresses spawning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 结果与复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14387v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2611.14387-b3/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e425de57d5146b0d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:b3" data-paper-title="Blurring the Block Boundaries: Overlapping Block Denoising for Efficient Diffusion Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-6eb0dee181596236">Do the gate and attention-invariance checks establish a diffusion decoder?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ab3">Blurring the Block Boundaries: Overlapping Block Denoising for Efficient Diffusion Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-11 · Technion / Amazon Web Services</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. The component consumes caller-supplied entropy, acceptance flags and EOS state and implements only the spawn gate and two-block mask. Native samplers, noise schedules, KV caches and a self-editing model are absent; synthetic inputs are not generated text.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Equal current-block outputs for random Q/K/V verify visibility only. They do not measure the paper&#x27;s ten-benchmark throughput or quality changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 数据协议与代码映射, 结果与复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14387v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2611.14387-b3/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6eb0dee181596236">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:real-loss" data-paper-title="REAL Loss: Optimizing Real Expected Acceptance Length for Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-real-loss-be9c2284" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9026210c47c40d75">Why is two-step speculative EAL not generally the product of two marginal acceptance rates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Areal-loss">REAL Loss: Optimizing Real Expected Acceptance Length for Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-12 · The University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The first accepted token determines the next prefix. Accepted branches are weighted by min(p,q), not simply target proportions. Ignoring covariance between branch survival and subsequent difficulty changes the objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: two drafts have the same first-step acceptance, but one puts accepted mass on easier continuations and the other on harder ones. Their true two-step EAL can differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14399">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2611.14399-real-loss/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9026210c47c40d75">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:real-loss" data-paper-title="REAL Loss: Optimizing Real Expected Acceptance Length for Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1636443b7a496bce">Why does REAL use q/p on target-sampled paths rather than serving acceptance p/q?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Areal-loss">REAL Loss: Optimizing Real Expected Acceptance Length for Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-12 · The University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A target path has sampling mass p. Multiplying by min(1,q/p) converts it to min(p,q), the accepted-branch mass. The branch estimator then replaces each prefix&#x27;s last sampled factor with full-vocabulary overlap a, while earlier W retains draft gradients.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: with p(A)=0.4 and q(A)=0.8, training weight one gives mass 0.4. Using p/q instead gives 0.2, no longer the accepted-branch mass.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与代码映射. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14399">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2611.14399-real-loss/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1636443b7a496bce">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:real-loss" data-paper-title="REAL Loss: Optimizing Real Expected Acceptance Length for Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-124ee1dee5611a5e">If REAL&#x27;s exact objective and WTV both equal 0.96, why aren&#x27;t they equivalent?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Areal-loss">REAL Loss: Optimizing Real Expected Acceptance Length for Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-12 · The University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>That equality holds at one parameter point. The exact expression 0.86+0.20theta increases with theta, whereas WTV&#x27;s 1.02−0.12theta decreases. Check definitions, expectations and gradients, not only a loss value.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: at theta=0.5 both are 0.96. At 0.6 the exact value rises to 0.98 while WTV falls to 0.948.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 论文离线与线上效果, 结果、负控与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14399">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2611.14399-real-loss/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-124ee1dee5611a5e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:real-loss" data-paper-title="REAL Loss: Optimizing Real Expected Acceptance Length for Speculative Decoding" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/generation-paths">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Generation paths: draft verification, parallel denoising, and few-step refinement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-aa5e1489af48d994">Why divide by three when a REAL window has only two valid positions before post-EOS masking?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Areal-loss">REAL Loss: Optimizing Real Expected Acceptance Length for Speculative Decoding</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-11-12 · The University of Hong Kong</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed gamma normalizes the paper&#x27;s objective. Masking removes post-EOS contributions without changing it into a random-length objective. Freeze target logits but retain gradients through prefix W and overlap a; callers must also establish real target-sampling provenance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Teaching example: with p=q and two valid positions, branch EAL is two, so pure EAL loss is 1−2/3. Dividing by valid length two incorrectly gives zero.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与代码映射, 结果、负控与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14399">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2611.14399-real-loss/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aa5e1489af48d994">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>

<details class="ar-learning-guide" markdown="1"><summary>Topic guide and reading order</summary>

## Start with this question

How can we reduce serial token generation while being explicit about whether the output distribution changes?

## Takeaway

Speculative decoding proposes several tokens with a cheap draft and verifies them in one target pass. Correct acceptance and residual correction preserve the target distribution. Diffusion language models instead denoise multiple positions; dQwen3.5 changes a causal backbone with recurrent layers to bidirectional propagation. Few-step generation and shared iterative networks change refinement schedules. These are changes at different levels.

## Example

A draft may propose four tokens and the target accept only the first two. The rest require correction and continued generation. Speed depends on acceptance and verification cost. A diffusion pass may update several positions, but multiple denoising passes can be needed. Compare full-output quality and end-to-end time, not tokens written in one pass.

## Common pitfall

Exact speculative sampling depends on the full acceptance and correction algorithm; it does not apply to arbitrary multihead drafts. Diffusion or distilled models are not automatically equivalent to the autoregressive target. Markov drafts, reference kernels, or call counts are not actual large-model speedups.

## Reading order

Start with the proposal, verification, and corrected sampling in Fast Inference. Then read dQwen3.5 on its bidirectional hybrid and parallel decoding. Distinguish rescheduling from training a new generative mechanism before exploring self-drafts, caching, and few-step refinements.

1. [Fast Inference from Transformers via Speculative Decoding](../../../../reproductions/2211.17192-speculative-decoding/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.17192)
2. [dQwen3.5: Adapting Hybrid Language Models into Bidirectional Diffusion Language Models](../../../../foundation-models/2609.20751-dqwen35/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20751)

## Check your understanding

Can “speculative decoding preserves the distribution” also describe changing an autoregressive backbone to diffusion?

??? note "Show suggested answer"

    No. Speculation reschedules computation under a fixed target distribution with acceptance and correction. Diffusion changes propagation, training, and decoding. It requires independent quality evaluation and cannot inherit that guarantee.

</details>
